purpose: Lanadelumab-flyo is used to help prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE), a condition that causes sudden, painful swelling in areas like the hands, feet, face, stomach, or throat. It is used in patients 12 years and older. This medication helps reduce how often these swelling attacks happen.
how_it_works: Your body has a protein called plasma kallikrein that, when overactive in HAE, triggers swelling attacks. Lanadelumab-flyo is a specially designed antibody that blocks this protein from becoming too active. By keeping plasma kallikrein in check, it helps prevent the chain reaction that leads to swelling episodes.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are pain, redness, or bruising at the injection site where the shot is given. Some people may also notice mild injection site reactions like itching or swelling right where the needle went in. These are usually mild and go away on their own.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you have signs of a serious allergic reaction such as hives, trouble breathing, swelling of the face or throat, or dizziness after your injection. This medication is given as an injection under the skin, so your healthcare provider will show you how to use it safely at home. Make sure to tell your doctor about all other medications you take and if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 300 mg injected under the skin (subcutaneous injection) once every 2 weeks. After your attacks are well controlled, your doctor may change your dose to 300 mg every 4 weeks. Your healthcare team will teach you or a caregiver how to give the injection at home.
